papers.title: Larger femoral periprosthetic bone mineral density decrease following total hip arthroplasty for femoral neck fracture than for osteoarthritis: A prospective, observational cohort study
papers.abstract: Studies on patients with degenerative joint disease of the hip show that femoral periprosthetic bone mineral decreases following total hip arthroplasty. Scarcely any osteodensitometric data exist on femoral neck fracture (FNF) patients and periprosthetic bone remodelling. In two parallel cohorts we enrolled 87 patients (mean age, 72 ± 12 years; male:female ratio, 30:57) undergoing total hip arthroplasty for either primary osteoarthritis (OA) of the hip (n = 37) or for an acute FNF (n = 50) and followed them for a mean of 5.4 years. Outcomes were bone mineral density (BMD) changes in the periprosthetic Gruen zones 1-7, the incidence of periprosthetic fractures and clinical outcome. The bone mineral loss in the fracture group was more than twice that of the osteoarthritis group, -16.9% versus -6.8% (p = 0.004). The incidence of periprosthetic fractures was 12% (6/50) in the fracture cohort compared with none (0%) in the OA cohort (p = 0.03). Periprosthetic bone mineral loss following total hip arthroplasty is significantly greater in patients who are treated for acute FNF than in OA patients. This decrease of BMD follows a different pattern with the FNF patients losing larger proportions of bone in Gruen zones 1, 2, 6, and 7 while the OA patients tend to have larger losses only in zones 1 and 7.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了全髋关节置换术后股骨假体周围骨密度变化，但未涉及应力遮挡或接触力学建模。
llm.why_not_core: This paper is a clinical observational study on BMD changes, not a biomechanical modeling or FEA study; it does not quantify stress shielding, micromotion, or implant-bone interface mechanics.

summary_zh.motivation: 比较股骨颈骨折与骨关节炎患者全髋置换后假体周围骨密度变化差异
summary_zh.method: 前瞻性队列研究，随访5.4年，测量Gruen区骨密度
summary_zh.result: 骨折组骨密度下降（-16.9%）显著大于骨关节炎组（-6.8%），骨折组假体周围骨折发生率更高
summary_zh.validation: 临床患者数据，双能X线吸收法测量骨密度

summary_en.motivation: To compare periprosthetic bone mineral density changes after total hip arthroplasty between patients with femoral neck fracture and those with osteoarthritis.
summary_en.method: A prospective observational cohort study with 87 patients followed for a mean of 5.4 years, measuring BMD in Gruen zones 1-7 using DXA.
summary_en.result: FNF patients showed significantly greater BMD loss (-16.9%) than OA patients (-6.8%), with a higher incidence of periprosthetic fractures (12% vs 0%).
summary_en.validation: Clinical cohort study with DXA measurements and fracture incidence tracking.
